name: neurarch-mcp
description: Before a training job takes a GPU: peak memory at its batch, the smallest card, max batch per card, the cost, and whether it forward-passes.
long_description: Call size_training_job before a training job launches and the agent learns what it actually needs: the training peak at its batch (weights and optimizer state, activations, stored attention scores), the smallest card that holds it, the largest batch each card holds, a two-card split when one card does not, and what one run costs. The number is a calibrated estimate under AdamW with bf16 autocast: fitted on 141 measured runs across 44 architectures, held-out median error 8% above 1 GB, and the fits / does-not-fit verdict on 16/24/40/80 GB cards agrees with measurement 98% of the time. Then whether it forward-passes: the design linter (lint_model) and the full readiness verdict (check_design), plus layers, parameters, FLOPs, 81 bundled reference architectures and runnable PyTorch export. All of that runs on your machine. Two tools reach the network when called: plan renders the same card the Neurarch CI bot posts, and history says what this exact structure measured the last time it trained inside your organisation.

model_path.title: Model file
model_path.description: A PyTorch .py file or a .neurarch.json graph. Try zoo:qwen2.5-7b for a bundled reference architecture.

tools.name: size_training_job
tools.description: Call before launching a training job: peak memory at your batch, smallest card that fits, max batch per card, two-card split, one run's cost. Calibrated, 8% median error.

tools.name: diagnose_oom
tools.description: Call after a CUDA out-of-memory error, before changing batch size: the one cause (too big, fragmented, another process, undeclared memory) and fixes, least invasive first.

tools.name: plan
tools.description: Will it run, what it costs, GPU fit, your .neurarch.yml rules, and what this structure scored last time it trained here.

tools.name: history
tools.description: What this exact structure scored the last time it trained in your organisation. Needs an API key.

tools.name: trace_model
tools.description: Run the model once in Python with hooks for a graph with real shapes.

tools.name: describe_architecture
tools.description: One-call orientation: pipeline, depth, params, MACs, hotspots, validation.

tools.name: lint_model
tools.description: The structural design rules, with provenance.

tools.name: check_design
tools.description: Readiness, cost, deployment fit and the decisions left to the human.

tools.name: rank_designs
tools.description: Order candidate designs; blocked last, ties stay ties, calibration included.

tools.name: layer_impact
tools.description: Blast radius of changing a layer.

tools.name: find_models
tools.description: Find model definitions in a repository.

prompts.name: review_design
prompts.description: A structured design review, every number from the tools.
prompts.text: Review the design of the current model: run describe_architecture, validate_model, lint_model and check_design, and report a verdict, the risks, and the edits worth making, every number from the tools.

prompts.name: pre_train_checklist
prompts.description: What to check before spending GPU time.
prompts.text: Run the pre-training checklist on the current model: graph well-formed, no blocking rule, warnings listed, forward pass runs, cost and GPU fit, shapes known, decisions still owed.

prompts.name: shrink_for_target
prompts.description: Fit a parameter, memory or latency budget with the least damage.
prompts.text: Bring the current model within this budget: {target}. Find where the budget lives, propose at most three variants, check each with layer_impact and rank them with rank_designs.

prompts.name: compare_with_reference
prompts.description: Put the model next to a published architecture.
prompts.text: Compare the current model with the reference architecture {architecture} from the bundled library: depth, width, attention configuration, normalisation, parameter distribution, and the rules that fire on one but not the other.

prompts.name: explain_finding
prompts.description: What a finding means and the smallest edit that clears it.
prompts.text: Explain the finding {rule} on the current model: what the rule checks, the evidence behind it, and the smallest edit that clears it with its blast radius.
